correctness.rationale: The three positive-descent reductions preserve residue modulo a=2n²+2n+1; terminal region L_n contains exactly a pairs and is residue-complete via the b-multiples since gcd(a,b)=1. Every nonterminal representative descends; any second representative has a last reversed reduction, so the least available reversal cost gives delta*n. Maximization over the three disjoint pieces gives 506 for n=3, 6n³+26n²+43n+22 for n=4,5, and 8n³+20n²+16n-2 for n>=6. Independent priority-queue enumeration of all coefficient pairs through the second Apéry threshold verified every residue and every formula for n=3..16; the general proof is the reduction argument, not enumeration.
